text: Friday morning: Black Hound holds a memorial. Kang Jaeha was a brave trap-tester, Mok tells the cameras. He always walked in first.
Hand on heart, Mok says Jaeha died so his hunters could come home. They will never forget him.
Out on the steps, Yoo Bomi, twenty-one, E-rank ranger and streamer of BomBom TV, works her camera drone like she owns the street.
She's here for clout: smash that like for the trap rat! Four hundred and twelve viewers. The chat types F.
And right past her walks the trap rat himself: bandaged, with Yerin and a small masked husk behind him.
Bomi does a huge double take.
She jumps in front of him with the drone. Isn't he the dead guy? Jaeha leans back, flustered, and finds the sky very interesting.
Nib just stares at her.
Jaeha bows and steps round her. Excuse him, miss. He's late for his own memorial.
The doors at the back of the hall swing open, and every head turns.
Yerin half hides behind his shoulder as the whole room stares.
At the podium, Mok freezes mid-word.
Jaeha walks up the aisle with a polite smile. Sorry he's late, sir. The rescue team kept him overnight.
Then he stands beside his own portrait and asks: could he say a few words at his memorial?
The room explodes, and Bomi's stream jumps to almost ten thousand. He's alive? This is staged. Summoners are still bait.
Mok recovers fast and crushes him in a bear hug for the cameras. His brave trap-tester! It's a miracle!
Then, through clenched teeth, right in his ear: back room. Now.
A small back office: Mok at the desk, the two hunters who got out with him, and Nib by the door like furniture.
He slides over a fat envelope. Sign a statement saying Jaeha set off the trap, and ten million won is his.
Jaeha gives him his politest smile. That's very generous, sir. Could he think about it until tomorrow?
Because in his chest pocket, his phone is recording. Not yet, sir.
Mok's smile is gone. Don't think too long. Trap rats get lost in gates all the time.
The crossbow hunter idly turns a brass compass with a violet crystal needle, studying the husk by the door.
Then Mok turns on Yerin. Sign as a witness, rookie, and she keeps her contract.
Her eyes go from fear to resolve.
She slaps her Black Hound contract card down on the statement. No. She watched him close that door. And she quits.
Nib pauses in the doorway and looks back at Mok: doors. You like closing them.
Mok goes slack with shock. Behind him, the crossbow hunter slowly smiles.
Alone, Mok crushes the statement in his fist.
Down the corridor, Black Hound hunters step out of their way, and one drops a paper cup.
That evening, home: a rooftop room in Mangwon-dong.
Kang Seoa, fifteen. His sister, who runs the household budget. She's crying and furious at once.
She pounds his chest. He said this was his last month of trap-testing! The news said he was dead, and all she got was one text at midnight!
Jaeha pulls her into a hug.
On the door behind them, a notice with a big red stamp.
Then she peeks over his arm. And who is that? And who is she?
Yerin bows too low: Song Yerin, who quit her job this morning. And that, Jaeha explains, is a very unusual husk.
Seoa runs the numbers. The landlady came today. Rent due: three hundred thousand won. Savings: zero. The school trip: unpaid.
Dinner is instant ramen with an egg in it. Nib's fingers hover over a bowl, and stop.
He pushes the bowl toward Jaeha. You first.
Seoa freezes, chopsticks halfway. Is his husk... eating?
Mouth full of noodles, Nib corrects her. He is not a husk. He is hungry.
Seoa and Yerin cling to each other while he slurps.
Then Jaeha stands up with a proud little smile. He got something from the boss. Watch this.
The Ninth Wall Blade drops out of the air and punches straight through the floor.
Jaeha ends up flat on his face beside it. You're weak, says Nib. Jaeha is aware.
Seoa's glasses flash. That's the landlady's floor!
Later that night, Jaeha leans alone on the railing, looking out over the river.
He turns the chain link in his hand. Somebody on this side put that knight in chains.
And on his phone, the recording from the back room.
Nib joins him with his ramen, bare feet dangling over the street. His sister is loud. She's the best person Jaeha knows.
Nib looks into his bowl, and his mouth almost softens. She makes good ramen.
Across the city, Kanghan Tower. Eleven forty-eight at night.
High in the tower, a man with a cane stands before a wall of monitors. Gate 0912. Boss core not harvested. Signal: Operator protocol.
Four faces on four screens: Mok, his shield-bearer, Yerin, and Jaeha.
And one signal spike, far above the rest.
Reflected in the dark glass: silver glasses and a polite smile. The survivors: Mok, his shield-bearer, a rookie healer, and a trap-tester who should be dead.
His hand tightens on his cane, a violet core glowing in the handle. Find out which one it is.
